title: Flat generic subgroup closure in a Dedekind lft-group
statement:
Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain, $E=\operatorname{Frac}D$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $M$ be a separated commutative $S$-group scheme, locally of finite type, and let $J\hookrightarrow M_E$ be a closed finite-type $E$-subgroup scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change, def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is a closed subgroup scheme $C\hookrightarrow M$, called the schematic closure of $J$, whose ideal on each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset M$ is
$$I_U=\ker\bigl(B\longrightarrow\Gamma(U_E\times_{M_E}J,\mathcal O)\bigr).$$
It is separated, commutative, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite type over $S$, and $C_E=J$ as closed subschemes of $M_E$. For every flat $S$-scheme $X$ and every $S$-morphism $f:X\to M$ whose generic restriction factors through $J$, there is a unique factorization $X\to C\hookrightarrow M$. A Dedekind domain means a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. A commutative group scheme over the indicated base has multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the commutative group diagrams, as in the field case [def-sc-group-scheme]; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Locally of finite type means that affine coordinate algebras are locally finitely generated over those of the base [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 4, proof, printed p.291 (PDF page 297), flat schematic subgroup closure; compare the finite-type version in 7.1 Corollary 6, printed p.175 (PDF page 181). Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Put $a:J\to M_E\to M$. For each affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset M$, its inverse image is the closed subscheme $J\times_{M_E}U_E$ of the affine $U_E=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_D E)$, hence is affine. Thus $a$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] to obtain its closed scheme-theoretic image $i:C\hookrightarrow M$ and the factorization of $a$. Since $a$ is quasi-compact, that node gives injectivity on sections of $\mathcal O_C\to a^{\mathrm{im}}_*\mathcal O_J$; over $C\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(B/\ker(a)(U))$ this says $B/\ker(a)(U)\to\Gamma(a^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_J)$ is injective, i.e. $\ker(a)(U)=\ker(B\to\Gamma(U_E\times_{M_E}J,\mathcal O))$, exactly the displayed ideal $I_U$. Its quasi-coherence supplies compatibility with restriction and gluing, so these quotients define one closed subscheme, even if $M$ is not quasi-compact.

source.place: Tags 01R6 and 01R8 (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image and lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image); affine inverse-image check

proof.text: Write $T=D\setminus\{0\}$, and let $K_U\subset T^{-1}B=B\otimes_D E$ be the ideal of $J\cap U_E$. Then $I_U$ is its contraction. Extension back to $T^{-1}B$ recovers $K_U$: if $b/t\in K_U$, then $b/1\in K_U$, hence $b\in I_U$; the reverse inclusion follows from the ideal property. Therefore $T^{-1}(B/I_U)=(T^{-1}B)/K_U$. These identifications respect the quotient maps and restrictions, proving $C_E=J$ as closed subschemes. Also $B/I_U$ injects into the $E$-algebra $(T^{-1}B)/K_U$ by the definition of $I_U$. For $0\ne d\in D$, if $d\bar b=0$ then its image is killed by the unit $d$ in that algebra, hence is zero and $\bar b=0$. Thus every displayed affine quotient is $D$-torsion-free.

source.place: Affine localization calculation in the construction of Tag 01R8

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dedekind-torsionfree-module-flat] to $B/I_U$ to obtain $D$-flatness. For $x\in C\cap U$, let $\mathfrak q$ be its prime in $B/I_U$ and $\mathfrak p$ its contraction to $D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], $D_{\mathfrak p}\to(B/I_U)_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat. These are precisely the local rings of $S$ and $C$ at the corresponding points. The affine charts $C\cap U$ cover $C$; the pointwise definition of flatness now proves $C\to S$ flat. No finite generation of a coordinate ring as a $D$-module was used.

Let $X$ and $f$ be as in the factorization clause. Cover $f^{-1}(U)$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The affine flatness criterion gives $A$ flat over $D$; [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] gives injectivity of every nonzero scalar. For $b\in I_U$, its pullback $f^\sharp(b)\in A$ becomes zero in $T^{-1}A$ because $f_E$ factors through $J$ and $b$ vanishes there. The defining equality of fractions gives $t f^\sharp(b)=0$ for some $t\in T$, so torsion-freeness gives $f^\sharp(b)=0$. The ring map therefore descends uniquely through $B/I_U$. The resulting maps $V\to C\cap U$ agree on overlaps: a morphism through a closed immersion is uniquely determined by its composite, since the sheaf map defining a closed immersion is surjective and its underlying space is a subspace. They glue to the required unique $X\to C$. This uses no quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis on $X$.

The identity base $S$ is flat over itself, since tensoring with $D$ is the identity. Both $C$ and $C\times_S C$ are flat over $S$: the projection $C\times_S C\to C$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and its composite with $C\to S$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-compose]. Apply Step 4 to $e_M:S\to M$, to $\operatorname{inv}_M\circ i:C\to M$, and to $m_M\circ(i\times i):C\times_S C\to M$. Their generic restrictions land in $J$, because $C_E=J$ and $J$ is a subgroup. This gives morphisms $e_C:S\to C$, $\operatorname{inv}_C:C\to C$ and $m_C:C\times_S C\to C$, compatible with $i$.

source.place: Agent extension of the closure construction: restrict the group operations using Step 4

proof.text: For associativity, compose both maps $C\times_S C\times_S C\to C$ with $i$. They become the two associative multiplication maps in $M$ and are equal. Cancel $i$ using uniqueness for maps through a closed immersion, proved in Step 4. Apply the same cancellation to the two unit equations, the two inverse equations and $m_C=m_C\circ\mathrm{swap}$. The corresponding equations hold in $M$. Thus these operations make $C$ a commutative $S$-group scheme and $i$ a subgroup immersion. This is the same definition as [def-sc-group-scheme], with the base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ replaced by $S$, explicitly stipulated in the item.

source.place: Group diagrams for the schematic closure, cancellation through its closed inclusion

proof.text: Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A'\subseteq S$ be any affine open. Since $M$ is locally of finite type, the preimage $M_V$ has an affine open cover by $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely generated $A'$-algebra; then $B/I_U$ is generated over $A'$ by the images of the same finite list. The opens $C\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I_U)$ cover $C_V$, giving local finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For separatedness, the inverse image of $\Delta_M$ under $C\times_S C\to M\times_S M$ is $C\times_M C=C$, since $i$ is a monomorphism. Its immersion is $\Delta_C$. A base change of a closed immersion is closed: on affine charts it is $A\to A/I$ tensored to $A'\to A'/IA'$, still surjective, with closed vanishing locus. Thus the closed diagonal of $M$ pulls back to a closed diagonal of $C$. Together with Steps 2–6 this proves every clause.

source.place: Affine quotient and diagonal arguments for inherited local finite type and separatedness
